To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we designed a SERS active gold nanozyme by growing AuNPs on a highly porous metal organic framework (MIL 101) and used it for monitoring the change in the levels of glucose and lactat in living tissues.

we designed a novel integrative nanozyme for in vitro and in vivo detection of glucose and lactic acid by combining AuNPs with both enzyme-mimicking and SERS activities, and that the nanozyme was further used for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of a potential drug (astaxanthin) and the metabolism of tumor in vivo.
we designed a perioxidase-mimicking nanozyme based on AuNPs@MOFs and used it for in vitro glucose and lactate sensing as well as in vivo imaging of these two metabolites in living brains and tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a new type of integrative nanozyme that combines the peroxidase mimetic activity and surface enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) activity of gold nanoparticles (AuNps) with the enzyme activity of glucose oxidase (Gox) for in vitro and in vivo monitoring of glucose.
the development of a novel SERS active nanozyme based on the combination of AuNP's intrinsic peroxidase mimetic activities with their SERS properties.
the development of a versatile SERS-active peroxidase mimetics (AuNPs@MOL-101) for in vitro glucose and lactate detection and in vivo monitoring of the change of glucose/lactate in living tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has provided a new strategy to design multifunctional nanoplatforms for versatile bioassay.

the integrative AuNPs@MOF@enzyme nanozymes were successfully designed for in vitro and in vivo SERS detection of glucose and lactic acid and for evaluating the efficacy of potential therapeutic drugs.
this work provides a novel strategy to design a multifunctional AuNPs@MOF nanozyme for SERS detection of glucose and L-lactate in living animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of the enzyme mimicking properties of AuNPs with their SERS activities provides a promising approach for developing versatile bioassay systems.
we designed an enzyme mimicking nanozymes by in situ growing gold nanoparticles (AuNPS) into a highly porous, thermally stable, and biocompatible metal organic framework MIL-101.
the AuNPs@porous metal organic framework nanozymes can be used as peroxidase and SERS active substrates for detecting glucose and lactate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can design and develop a multifunctional nanozyme by combining AuNPs with a porous metal organic framework.
we have designed an integrative nanozyme that combines peroxidase mimetics and SERS activity, which is a new strategy for designing multifunctional nanomaterials.
we have developed a new type of SERS-active nanozyme by growing AuNPs onto a highly porous metal-organic framework MIL 101.
